Business goal: Create a reusable non-root auth principal for a verified tenant-admin without tying authentication permanently to the tenant-admin row.
User outcome: A verified tenant-admin redemption can provision a shared login identity that can later be reused across multiple tenant-scoped roles or memberships.
Notes / constraints: This remains the bridge between the tenantAdmins auth-ready slice and the shared tenant-auth model, but the public handoff now happens at verification redemption rather than through a standalone tenant-auth bootstrap route. Principal email must remain globally unique across non-root principals. The source tenant-admin must be verified and active. This slice should still support future tenant users without introducing a second auth system.
Tenant context rule: no active tenant session exists yet; creation is identity provisioning from a verified tenant-admin record rather than an in-session tenant action
Explicitly denied roles: unauthenticated callers; unverified tenant admins; deleted tenant admins; future tenant users not yet linked to a verified source actor
Authorization summary: This capability is feature-owned by tenantAuth but is triggered by verified tenant-admin redemption in tenantAdmins. It should not be modeled as a tenant-admin login itself.
Authz scope type: shared principal provisioning over one verified tenant-admin subject and one global login email
Frontend visibility rule: Future onboarding screens will depend on this but no UI is required in this loop.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce verified active source-actor eligibility and global principal-email uniqueness before creating principal linkage and credential placeholders.
Request contract: Body includes the raw tenant-admin verification token only. Client-supplied principalId sessionId tenant membership or password hash fields are rejected.
Response contract: Returns verified tenant-admin state plus tenantAuthOnboarding with authPrincipalId loginEmail passwordSetupRequired bootstrapToken and nextStep. No authenticated tenant session is created by this capability alone.
Error contract: 400 invalid verification token; 410 expired token; 409 already verified or already consumed state when applicable.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on tenantAdmins public seam for verified subject lookup and on shared email-normalization rules. Must remain compatible with future tenant-user and membership onboarding.
Persistence impact: Insert durable shared principal row plus durable linkage from principal to the source tenant-admin actor or future shared membership abstraction.
Indexes / uniqueness: Global unique index on normalized login email. Unique principal-to-source linkage rule for the current verified subject. Secondary lookup indexes by source actor id and active state.
Search / filter model: No search surface required in v1; exact verification redemption only.
Session / auth dependency: No existing tenant session is required. This is pre-login identity provisioning.
Compatibility / migration notes: Keep the auth principal separate from tenant-admin profile records so future tenant users and multi-tenant memberships reuse the same identity layer.
Authentication requirement: No authenticated tenant session required; valid verification token required.
Authorization enforcement layer: Feature-local validation plus future shared auth middleware at the verification-redemption boundary.
CSP / browser security impact: Design request and response shapes so browser onboarding can call them later without API redesign.
Audit requirement: Audit successful provisioning and denied attempts with source actor tenantId tenantAdminId principalId when known and outcome reason.
Privacy / personal data impact: High; creates durable non-root identity records and login email ownership.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authentication controls plus privacy review for globally unique login identity and source-actor linkage.
Acceptance notes: The result is one reusable non-root auth principal with a globally unique login email and no tenant session yet.

Business goal: Allow a newly bootstrapped shared tenant principal to set its first password after successful onboarding.
User outcome: A newly verified tenant-admin can create their first password and complete account setup without using a root-managed credential path.
Notes / constraints: This is initial password set not forgot-password reset. The source principal must exist and be in a password-not-yet-set or onboarding-required state. Password policy should align with platform baseline and remain reusable for future tenant users. This route should be frontend-ready for future onboarding forms.
Tenant context rule: no active tenant context required; password setup happens before or alongside the first login flow
Allowed root roles: RootUserAdmin for support override if explicitly designed; normal caller is onboarding principal
Minimum role required: System onboarding proof or unauthenticated proof flow
Explicitly denied roles: authenticated tenant sessions for unrelated principals; callers without valid onboarding proof; deleted or disabled source actors
Authorization summary: This is a shared auth capability for tenant-side identities and must not live under tenantAdmins. It creates credentials for the principal layer only.
Authz scope type: shared onboarding credential bootstrap over one principal
Frontend visibility rule: Future onboarding UI will depend on this and needs stable validation and error codes.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce valid bootstrap/onboarding proof principal eligibility password policy and single-use semantics before writing the password hash and clearing onboarding-required state.
Request contract: Body includes onboarding proof or bootstrap token plus newPassword and repeated password confirmation if the contract decides to validate repeat client-side and server-side. Client cannot supply passwordHash principalId lifecycle fields or tenant selection data.
Response contract: Returns minimal setup-complete payload such as authPrincipalId loginEmail passwordSet=true and a user-safe next-step hint. No tenant session has to be created automatically unless the final PRD chooses that path explicitly.
Error contract: 400 invalid password payload; 401 invalid or missing onboarding proof; 409 password already set; 410 expired onboarding proof; 422 policy violation.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on shared principal bootstrap state and rootAuth-like password hashing rules but must remain separate from rootAuth implementation details where business semantics differ.
Persistence impact: Insert durable password-credential row or update principal credential state with a hashed password and setup timestamps.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique principal credential ownership. Indexes by principalId and active credential state. Password hash storage and policy constraints must be explicit.
Search / filter model: No general search surface. Exact onboarding proof only.
Session / auth dependency: No tenant session required yet though the later login flow may follow immediately after setup.
Compatibility / migration notes: Design so future tenant users use the same password-setup path and so forgot-password reset can target the same credential ownership model later.
Authentication requirement: No active tenant session required; valid onboarding/bootstrap proof required.
Authorization enforcement layer: Feature-local onboarding proof validation plus shared credential storage rules.
CSP / browser security impact: Frontend-ready validation and errors should support future browser onboarding without changing contract semantics later.
Audit requirement: Audit successful setup and denied attempts with principalId when known source actor linkage when known and outcome reason.
Privacy / personal data impact: High; handles credential creation and sensitive identity state.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS credential storage and onboarding-flow controls.
Acceptance notes: Initial password setup creates reusable principal credentials without issuing role-specific auth identities.

Business goal: Authenticate a non-root tenant principal by globally unique email and password and establish a server-backed tenant session bootstrap state.
User outcome: A tenant actor can sign in with email and password and receive either an active tenant session for one accessible tenant or a tenant-selection-required result when multiple tenant contexts exist.
Notes / constraints: Email is globally unique across non-root principals. Login should be frontend-ready and return deterministic states for: invalid credentials, inactive principal, onboarding incomplete, single tenant auto-selection, or multiple-tenant selection required. Sessions are server-backed for now.
Tenant context rule: tenant is chosen after login from accessible contexts; if exactly one context exists selection is skipped and the session resolves automatically
Explicitly denied roles: unauthenticated callers without valid credentials; principals without active tenant access; principals still awaiting onboarding completion
Authorization summary: This is the main non-root login capability and must remain reusable across tenant-admins and future tenant users with narrower roles.
Authz scope type: shared login capability over one principal and its accessible tenant contexts
Frontend visibility rule: Future browser login and app login surfaces will depend on this route and its stable state machine.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce principal lookup password verification active-state checks and tenant-access resolution before creating or returning session state. Do not leak whether an email exists beyond the approved error model.
Frontend states: idle, submitting, invalid credentials, onboarding required, selection required, authenticated, locked out
Session / expiry behavior: Server-backed session is created on successful login. If exactly one tenant context exists the session can be resolved immediately to that tenant. If multiple exist the session may be created in an authenticated-but-unselected state awaiting tenant choice.
Client-side permission behavior: Client should treat the returned accessible-tenant list and session state as the authoritative source for whether tenant selection is needed.
Request contract: Body includes email and password only in v1. Client-supplied tenantId role or session fields are rejected.
Response contract: Returns one of: authentication failure; onboarding required; selection required with available tenant contexts; or authenticated session with active tenant context when only one tenant is accessible.
Error contract: 400 invalid payload; 401 invalid credentials; 403 principal inactive or not eligible; 409 onboarding incomplete; 429 throttled.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on shared principal and credential ownership model and on durable principal-to-tenant access linkage. Must stay separate from rootAuth and tenantAdmins lifecycle routes.
Persistence impact: Insert durable tenant session row and durable login audit evidence. No tenant-admin row mutation on successful login.
Indexes / uniqueness: Global unique principal email lookup. Secondary indexes on session ids principal ids and active session expiry windows.
Search / filter model: No general search surface in v1; exact email login only.
Session / auth dependency: Creates or reads server-backed tenant session state.
Compatibility / migration notes: Keep response states browser-ready so a future frontend can render tenant-selection or direct entry without API redesign. Avoid hard-coding tenant-admin-specific assumptions into login semantics.
Authentication requirement: Public unauthenticated login entrypoint with valid credentials required.
Authorization enforcement layer: Feature-local auth validation plus shared abuse controls and later tenant session middleware.
CSP / browser security impact: Frontend-ready auth route should be compatible with future cookie or bearer transport choices without changing outcome semantics.
Audit requirement: Audit successful and denied logins with principalId when known ip user agent resolved tenant-count and whether selection was required.
Privacy / personal data impact: High; handles credentials session bootstrap and tenant-access metadata.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authentication and session-management controls.
Acceptance notes: Successful login either auto-selects a single tenant or returns a selection-required result with accessible tenant contexts.

Business goal: Read the current authenticated tenant session including active tenant context and whether tenant selection is still required.
User outcome: A signed-in tenant actor can refresh the app and recover whether they are authenticated which principal they are and which tenant context is active or still pending selection.
Notes / constraints: This is the tenant-side equivalent of current-session read and should be designed for future frontend bootstrap. Response should include principal summary active tenant context when selected and available tenant contexts or a count when selection is required.
Tenant context rule: returns current active tenant context if selected; otherwise indicates selection required and exposes available tenant contexts for chooser UI
Explicitly denied roles: unauthenticated callers; expired or revoked sessions; callers attempting to force a different tenant via this route
Authorization summary: Session read is shared and reusable across all future tenant actor types. It must not expose root-only data or tenant-admin lifecycle internals unnecessarily.
Authz scope type: shared current-session read over one authenticated principal session
Frontend visibility rule: Future frontend app shell will depend on this for bootstrapping and refresh continuity.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce session validity and return only tenant contexts linked to the authenticated principal. Do not allow route params or body data to override active tenant context.
Frontend states: loading, authenticated, selection required, unauthenticated, expired
Session / expiry behavior: Reads existing server-backed session and its current tenant selection state without mutating it.
Client-side permission behavior: Client should trust the server-returned active tenant and accessible contexts rather than caching stale local assumptions.
Request contract: No body. Authenticated tenant session required.
Response contract: Returns session summary including authPrincipalId loginEmail activeTenant when selected session expiry and availableTenantContexts or selectionRequired flag.
Error contract: 401 invalid or expired session; 429 throttled if shared session-read abuse posture is later applied.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on shared principal session store and tenant-access linkage. Must stay compatible with future browser shell and API clients.
Persistence impact: Read durable tenant session state and any linked active tenant selection metadata.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on sessionId principalId and expiry timestamps. Tenant-selection lookup may rely on principal-to-tenant linkage indexes.
Search / filter model: No general search surface. Exact current-session read only.
Compatibility / migration notes: Keep this response stable enough for a future frontend bootstrap shell and do not couple it to tenant-admin-specific profile fields.
Authorization enforcement layer: Shared tenant-session middleware plus feature-local response assembly.
CSP / browser security impact: Frontend-ready shell bootstrap route; no special CSP requirement beyond future cookie transport compatibility.
Audit requirement: Audit denied session reads and optionally successful session reads if later policy requires tenant-side session visibility logs.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate to high; returns identity and tenant-access metadata to the authenticated actor only.
Acceptance notes: Session read truthfully reports whether the actor is authenticated and whether tenant selection is still pending.

Business goal: List the tenant contexts a principal can access after authentication so the client can render a tenant chooser when needed.
User outcome: An authenticated principal with access to multiple tenants can see a stable list of allowed tenant contexts and choose the right workspace.
Notes / constraints: This route may be folded into session read if the final PRD prefers a single bootstrap response, but the capability should still be represented explicitly. It must be reusable across tenant-admin and future tenant-user actor types. Returned contexts should be enough for a chooser UI without leaking unrelated internal authorization records.
Tenant context rule: lists only tenant contexts linked to the authenticated principal; no route-supplied tenantId required
Explicitly denied roles: unauthenticated callers; principals whose sessions are invalid; callers requesting contexts they do not own
Authorization summary: List availability is shared across all future tenant actors and is a core part of the multi-tenant user model.
Authz scope type: shared authenticated list capability over all tenant contexts linked to one principal
Frontend visibility rule: Future tenant chooser UI depends on this and needs stable labels and identifiers.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce authenticated session validity and derive contexts only from durable principal-to-tenant access linkage.
Frontend states: loading, empty access, single tenant, multiple tenants
Session / expiry behavior: Reads authenticated session and linked access contexts; no mutation.
Client-side permission behavior: Client should treat the returned list as authoritative and must not infer access from stale cached tenant memberships.
Request contract: No body. Authenticated tenant session required.
Response contract: Returns ordered accessible tenant contexts with tenantId display label actor/profile summary role summary and whether one is currently active.
Error contract: 401 invalid session; 403 no tenant access if the final model distinguishes that from unauthenticated; 429 throttled if later policy applies.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on durable principal-to-tenant linkage and on tenant profile summary seams from tenantAdmins first and later tenant-user features.
Persistence impact: Read durable principal-to-tenant access linkage and optional active selection metadata.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on principal-to-tenant linkage by principalId and active state. Ordering and lookup rules should be deterministic for chooser UX.
Compatibility / migration notes: Design the returned tenant-context shape so future tenant-user roles and profile variants fit without changing the route contract.
Authorization enforcement layer: Shared tenant-session middleware plus feature-local context-assembly rules.
CSP / browser security impact: Frontend-ready chooser route with no special CSP requirement beyond future browser compatibility.
Audit requirement: Audit denied attempts and optionally successful chooser reads if tenant-access visibility needs become compliance-relevant later.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; reveals which tenants a principal can access and role/display context metadata.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and privacy controls for tenant-scoped access visibility.
Acceptance notes: Returned tenant contexts are sufficient for a future chooser UI and remain reusable for future tenant-user roles.

Business goal: Select the active tenant context for an already authenticated principal who can access more than one tenant.
User outcome: An authenticated principal can choose which tenant workspace they want to enter and the session will persist that active tenant until changed or cleared.
Notes / constraints: This capability is skipped when the principal has access to exactly one tenant and login auto-selects it. Selection should be idempotent and safe. It should update server-backed session state only after validating that the requested tenant belongs to the authenticated principal's allowed contexts.
Tenant context rule: sets or changes the active tenant context on the existing authenticated session
Explicitly denied roles: unauthenticated callers; principals requesting tenants they cannot access; callers trying to select deleted or unavailable tenant contexts
Authorization summary: This is the tenant-context switch capability for shared non-root auth and should remain reusable across future actor types and tenant roles.
Authz scope type: shared authenticated exact mutation over one allowed tenant context
Frontend visibility rule: Future tenant chooser UI depends on this for multi-tenant principals.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce session validity and durable tenant-access ownership before mutating active tenant selection state.
Frontend states: submitting, selected, invalid choice, session expired
Session / expiry behavior: Mutates existing server-backed session to record the active tenant context. Session expiry follows normal tenant-session policy.
Client-side permission behavior: Client should treat the server-returned active tenant context as authoritative after selection and update local shell state from the response.
Request contract: Body includes tenantId only. Client-supplied role claims or profile fields are rejected.
Response contract: Returns updated session summary with active tenant context resolved and selectionRequired=false.
Error contract: 400 invalid payload; 401 invalid session; 403 tenant not accessible to the principal; 404 tenant context not found when safe; 409 selection not needed if auto-selected single-tenant mode already applies.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on durable principal-to-tenant linkage and on a lightweight tenant-context summary seam. Must remain compatible with future tenant browser shell and API clients.
Persistence impact: Update durable session state with active tenant selection fields and timestamps.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on sessionId plus activeTenantId and principal-to-tenant linkage lookup by principalId and tenantId.
Compatibility / migration notes: Keep the selected-tenant semantics stable so future frontend shells and later finer-grained tenant roles do not need a contract rewrite.
Authorization enforcement layer: Shared tenant-session middleware plus feature-local access verification.
CSP / browser security impact: Frontend-ready chooser submission route; future browser UX may call this immediately after login when multiple tenants are available.
Audit requirement: Audit successful selection changes and denied attempts with principalId requested tenantId previous active tenant when known and outcome reason.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; mutates tenant workspace context for an authenticated actor and may influence downstream authorization decisions.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS session and authorization controls for tenant context switching.
Acceptance notes: Selection updates the server-backed session only when the requested tenant is in the principal's allowed context list.

Business goal: End the current authenticated tenant session cleanly.
User outcome: A tenant actor can sign out and clear the current server-backed session regardless of whether a tenant was selected.
Notes / constraints: This should be the tenant-side equivalent of logout and stay frontend-ready for future browser and app clients. It should not mutate tenant-admin profile or shared principal state beyond session revocation.
Tenant context rule: clears current active tenant context as part of session termination because the whole authenticated session ends
Explicitly denied roles: unauthenticated callers; expired or already-revoked sessions if the final contract treats those as invalid
Authorization summary: Logout is shared across all future tenant actors because the authenticated identity and session are shared.
Authz scope type: shared authenticated self-logout over current tenant session
Frontend visibility rule: Future frontend app shell depends on this for session teardown and redirect behavior.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce valid current session and revoke it durably. Clear active-tenant selection implicitly by ending the session rather than storing a stale context.
Session / expiry behavior: Revokes current server-backed session. Later browser transport can map this to cookie clearing without changing route semantics.
Client-side permission behavior: Client should clear local cached session and tenant-context state only after the server confirms logout or when the session is already invalid.
Request contract: No body. Authenticated tenant session required.
Response contract: Returns minimal logout result with session revoked=true and client-safe next-step guidance.
Error contract: 401 invalid or expired session; 429 throttled if later policy applies.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on shared tenant session store and later browser transport rules but should not depend on tenantAdmins or specific tenant role features.
Persistence impact: Durably revoke current tenant session and preserve logout audit evidence.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on sessionId principalId and revocation timestamps.
Search / filter model: No search surface. Current-session mutation only.
Compatibility / migration notes: Design logout semantics so future browser-cookie transport can reuse the same server-side session revocation path without API redesign.
Authorization enforcement layer: Shared tenant-session middleware plus feature-local logout handler.
CSP / browser security impact: Frontend-ready logout route should remain compatible with future cookie clearing and browser redirect flows.
Audit requirement: Audit successful logout and denied attempts with principalId active tenant when known and outcome reason.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; touches session and tenant-context state but not credential ownership.
Acceptance notes: Logout revokes the current server-backed tenant session cleanly without mutating profile or principal ownership state.
